key_insight: UltraQuant shows that 4-bit KV caching can preserve agent quality while substantially improving latency and throughput in long-context, multi-turn workloads.
engineering_relevance: For serving context-heavy agents, KV-cache compression is not just a memory optimization but a systems-level lever for keeping GPUs busy and reducing time-to-first-token under concurrency.
method: Use 4-bit KV-cache quantization tailored to multi-round agent traces
Apply rotation/codebook techniques with asymmetric K/V handling, Walsh-Hadamard rotation, and block-scale variants
Deploy AMD GPU serving optimizations, including optimized decode-attention kernels and an FP4 UltraQuant path with FP8 queries and UE8M0 group scales
evidence_signal: On a long-context, multi-turn agentic workload, UltraQuant achieved a 3.47x P50 time-to-first-token improvement in cache-pressured late rounds and 1.63x higher output throughput versus the FP8 KV baseline.
watch_item: The approach depends on specialized kernel support and hardware features, so portability and stability across different GPU platforms may be a practical constraint.
paper_title: UltraQuant: 4-bit KV Caching for Context-Heavy Agents
